name_en: Hamo no yakimono — grilled pike conger, a fixture of Kyoto's Gion Festival table
summary_ja: 小骨の多いハモに熟練の「骨切り」を施し、醤油だれの照り焼きや塩焼きにする京料理。生きたまま京都まで運べる生命力の強さから内陸の京都に根づいたとされ、「はも祭り」とも呼ばれる祇園祭の行事食でもある。
summary_en: Pike conger, riddled with fine bones, is scored with the skilled honekiri cut and then grilled — teriyaki-glazed or salted — in Kyoto cuisine. Said to have taken root in landlocked Kyoto because the hardy fish could be carried in alive, it is also a festival food for Gion Matsuri, nicknamed the 'hamo festival.'
source_title: はもの焼き物 京都府 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Kamonasu dengaku — Kyoto's round eggplant, pan-fried and topped with sweet miso
summary_ja: 直径10cmを超え「なすの女王」とも呼ばれる京野菜「賀茂なす」を輪切りにして油でじっくり焼き、酒・みりん・砂糖で煮詰めた田楽味噌をのせる。上賀茂の扇状地で古くから育てられてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: Kamonasu, a round Kyoto heirloom eggplant over 10cm across sometimes called the 'queen of eggplants,' is sliced and pan-fried in plenty of oil, then topped with a sweet miso reduced with sake and mirin. It is said to have long been grown on the alluvial fan of Kamigamo.
source_title: 賀茂なすの田楽 京都府 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
